agree.reason: Saying plainly that traffic will get worse, then offering a condition on the intersection, gives the two commissioners worried about traffic a way to vote yes, though most of the opposing neighbours probably won't change their minds.

honest.reason: Most claims stick to the brief, but "house 64 of those households" assumes the tenants will come from the waiting list, which the brief doesn't say, and 64 of 412 is closer to one in 6.4 than one in six.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out new figures, including the share of the waiting list, the eight spare parking spaces and the trade-off if nothing changes, but it leaves the 310 trips as a raw daily total when a per-unit or rush-hour figure would sound smaller.

right_comparison.reason: It describes saying no as the facts support it: the lot stays empty six days a week, 412 households keep waiting about three years, and 64 homes are lost.

qualification.reason: The proposed condition to review signal timing names the intersection, but it gives no deadline, no rating to aim for and no consequence if the review isn't done, so the commission can't check it.

objections.reason: It meets the main objection, traffic, head-on and deals with parking using the brief's own numbers, without raising any objection the facts don't support.

fit.reason: At about 400 words, it's a first-person public comment that fits a three-minute slot when spoken.
